--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Connection pool exhaustion on serverless deployments
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L30)
Evidence: PrismaClient is instantiated as a process-global singleton but datasource is PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL with no pooling/proxy indicated; code relies on the Node process cache only. In a serverless Next.js environment this still creates one DB connection pool per function/container and will open many connections under concurrency.  
Impact: At modest concurrency (≈50 concurrent serverless invocations on small DB plans) the DB's max_connections will be exhausted causing connection errors and timeouts (connection pool exhaustion / DB CPU/IOPS spikes).  
Fix: Front Prisma with a connection pooler (PgBouncer/Proxy) or use a serverless-safe pooling strategy (Neon serverless/pgbouncer + set connection limits), and tune Prisma connection limits.

[DB-2] Trade + ledger writes not atomic (financial inconsistency)
File: actions/trade.ts (L180-L260)
Evidence: addTrade creates a Trade record then calls createTradeEntryFund inside a try/catch and continues even if fund creation fails; same pattern exists for exits/pyramids (createTradePyramid & createTradeExit call fund creation and swallow failures).  
Impact: Creates irreversible divergence between trade records and the funds ledger (missing or out-of-sync fund entries) — financial inconsistency that can occur under partial failures or transient DB errors, leading to incorrect balances and unrecoverable data loss.  
Fix: Wrap trade + corresponding fund writes (and subsequent status/avg recalcs) in a single DB transaction (prisma.$transaction) or use a reliable, transactional queue / compensating transaction ensuring both succeed or the operation fully rolls back.

[DB-3] Race conditions when modifying same trade (lost updates)
File: actions/trade-pyramid.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: createTradePyramid creates a pyramid row, then separately calls recalculateTradeStatus and recalculateAverageEntryPrice (both perform separate reads/updates) without using transactions or row-level locking. Concurrent pyramids/exits against the same trade will interleave reads/updates.  
Impact: Concurrent modifications to the same trade (e.g., multiple exits/pyramids) can produce incorrect displayQuantity, averageEntryPrice, and status; this breaks correctness even at low parallelism (≈5–10 concurrent writes against one trade), causing data inconsistency and incorrect trading state.  
Fix: Perform the create + status/avg recalculation inside a single transaction or use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to serialize per-trade updates.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Unbounded user-facing findMany (no pagination)
File: actions/trade.ts (getAllTrades) (L300-L380)
Evidence: getAllTrades and getTradeStats call prisma.tradeLog.findMany (include pyramids/exits) without take/limit/cursor pagination, returning every trade for the user.  
Impact: Users with many trades (thousands) will cause large result sets to be read and processed in-memory, increasing DB CPU/IOPS and request latency; scale pain appears as DB reads and response times spike (problematic above hundreds–thousands of rows).  
Fix: Add cursor/limit pagination or server-side caps and fetch lightweight projections for list endpoints.

[DB-5] Large OR-list queries for live/closing prices
File: actions/trade.ts (getCurrentMarketPrices) (L780-L980)
Evidence: Builds a large OR array of {symbol,exchange,segment} and passes it to prisma.findMany; for many symbols this produces a huge OR-list query.  
Impact: With hundreds of symbols this causes large query planning time and IOPS, and can push DB CPU/latency higher (degrades at hundreds of symbols per request).  
Fix: Batch symbol lookups, use indexed IN queries on single columns (or a temporary values table / join), or limit request symbol count and cache results.

[DB-6] Sequential DB writes in bulk imports (slow & transactional risk)
File: actions/trade.ts (bulkImportTrades) (L420-L620)
Evidence: bulkImportTrades processes rows in a for-loop and awaits each createTrade/createPyramid/createExit sequentially (no batching or transaction grouping).  
Impact: Large imports are slow and increase DB transaction count; partial failures mid-import can leave partially-applied sets (consistency and long-running connection pressure).  
Fix: Batch writes where possible and use per-import transactions or a background job to apply records with retries/atomicity.

--- INFO ---

[DB-7] Schema has thoughtful indexes
File: prisma/schema.prisma (model definitions/indexes)
Evidence: Multiple @@index and @@unique declarations exist for high-traffic columns (userId/profileId/status, symbol+exchange+segment, daily_close unique keys).
